status.en: 11 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 27% fewer than the week before, most of them in Caracas, Valencia and Llano Alto.
status.nb: 11 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 27 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Caracas, Valencia og Llano Alto.

summary.en: US has taken a fugitive businessman into custody in Venezuela on bribery charges, while Maduro and Flores face formal US charges for ordering torture, sparking protests. An aid worker describes earthquake damage in Venezuela as shocking, and Rubio calls on all opposition figures to join talks with the government. Starlink internet is now allowed to operate in Venezuela and Cuba’s grid collapse is worsening regional strain. Energy firms are recruiting former US officials to access Venezuelan oil, and charges against Maduro allege a PDVSA plane was used to transport goods. There were 2 battle-related deaths in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: USA har tatt en flyktig forretningsmann i forvaring i Venezuela på bestikkelsesanklage, mens Maduro og Flores står overfor formelle amerikanske anklager for å ha beordret tortur, noe som har utløst protester. En hjelpearbeider beskriver jordskade i Venezuela som sjokkerende, og Rubio oppfordrer alle opposisjonsfigurer til å delta i samtaler med regjeringen. Starlink-internett får nå lov til å operere i Venezuela, og Cubas strømbrudd forverrer den regionale spenningen. Energibedrifter rekrutterer tidligere amerikanske tjenestemenn for å få tilgang til venezuelansk olje, og anklagene mot Maduro hevder at et PDVSA-fly ble brukt til å transportere varer. Det var 2 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
